q: The Nasdaq rose 6.51% while the Dow rose only 3.01%. What best explains the gap?
options: The Fed's Williams hinted at lower rates for tech
Money chased tech and AI first after Huang's return
Investors sold tech to buy the Dow's steadier names
Falling oil hurt the industrial firms in the Dow
explain: The Nasdaq leans toward tech, and Nvidia's jump drove the day. The order Nasdaq, S&P 500, Dow shows money chased AI first.

q: Last week yields fell on AI worries. Today the S&P 500 rose 4.73% but the 10-year yield rose only 1 bp. What does that suggest?
options: Bond traders were waiting for the ECB's collateral rules
Oil's drop to 80.38 cancelled out the stock rally
Bonds had already priced the full AI rebound last week
Bonds were driven by Fed rate talk more than AI mood
explain: Safe-haven buying eased, yet yields barely moved. The Fed's hike signals from Williams were the stronger force for bonds.

q: The Fed surprises with a hike signal while inflation comes mainly from oil. The gap between the 10-year and 2-year yield, now +29 bp, would probably go which way?
options: Up
Down
explain: The San Francisco Fed paper says surprises pass through less to long yields when inflation is supply-driven. So the 2-year rises more than the 10-year and the gap shrinks.

q: WTI fell 4.29% to its lowest settle since August because the attacks on tankers stopped.
options: True
False
explain: Tanker attacks are still happening. Oil fell because crude kept flowing out of the Gulf despite them.

q: Gold rose 3.26% to 3629.9 while the VIX fell 25.83%. What is the honest reading from today's headlines?
options: The headlines give no cause, so it stays unexplained
Oil's drop to 80.38 pushed buyers into gold instead
A weaker dollar made gold cheaper for foreign buyers
Fear rose in other markets, so buyers hid in gold
explain: Gold usually gains on fear, but fear fell today. The dollar also rose, so the cheaper-gold story fails. The debrief says the cause is unclear.

q: Kroger and Tyson fell today as money rushed into AI. If the AI trade wobbles next week, what would these defensive stocks probably do?
options: Up
Down
explain: Today's selling was a swap out of safe names into AI. If AI wobbles, some money would likely flow back to the safe names.

q: Put today's stock chain in order, from cause to effect.
explain: The news lifts Nvidia first. Nvidia's weight in the index lifts the S&P 500, and a calmer market pulls the VIX down.

q: Put today's oil chain in order, from cause to effect.
items: Gulf oil keeps flowing despite attacks
explain: Supply keeps arriving, so traders worry less and the price drops. Cheaper fuel then feeds into lower headline inflation.

q: The 2-year yield of 4.63% sits above the Fed's 3.875% rate, which hints that markets already expect some hikes.
options: True
False
explain: The 2-year yield tracks expected Fed rates. A yield well above the current rate means traders expect the Fed to raise it.

q: Williams said higher rates are likely 'over time' but expects inflation near 2% in 2027. What is the best reading?
options: The Fed expects hikes to push inflation higher into 2027
The Fed would hike over time and expect relief by 2027
The Fed sees oil as demand-driven, so the jump will last
The Fed plans cuts soon because inflation is nearly beaten
explain: He leans toward more hikes now and expects inflation to move closer to the 2% target in 2027. Oil is a supply shock, not a demand one.

q: The dollar index rose 0.49% to 104.32 on a day the Nasdaq rose 6.51%. Which explanation fits best?
options: Hawkish Fed bets outweighed the usual risk-on dip in the dollar
Japan's intervention forced extra dollar buying by Tokyo today
Fresh midterm election news drove heavy dollar buying today
Goldman's call for a 2027 pullback pulled buyers in today
explain: Headlines tie the dollar's rally to hawkish Fed bets, not the election. Japan's intervention means selling dollars, so it points the other way.

q: Members of both parties questioned Trump's view of Huang and Bessent reversed his harder line. Why does this matter for a market that rose 4.73%?
options: Bessent's reversal ends tariffs, which would hit the dollar
Congress sets the Fed's rate, so hikes could follow
The rally leans on one firm, so action could remove it
Any criticism pushes the VIX higher automatically each day
explain: Today's rally rests heavily on Nvidia's story. Political or legal action, like the reported SEC probe, could remove that support.

q: Kroger and Tyson were among the S&P 500's biggest losers while Nvidia soared. What does that suggest?
options: Rate hike talk hit only food firms and nobody else
Investors sold safer defensive names to buy AI shares
Shoppers cut grocery spending after the stock rally
Falling oil raised the costs of food producers today
explain: Consumer stocks were seen as a safe bet during the AI cracks. When AI recovered, money moved out of them and into tech.

q: A New York Fed post says US working-age population growth is near zero. How could that keep the Fed hawkish even if oil falls?
options: Scarce workers push up wages, so service prices stay sticky
Fewer workers cut oil demand, so oil would rebound
Fewer workers weaken the dollar, so imports cost more
Fewer workers shrink bank reserves, lifting funding costs
explain: Fewer available workers means employers compete for them and wages can rise. That keeps services inflation sticky even when fuel gets cheaper.

q: Nvidia's financing of Oracle and CoreWeave suddenly looks shaky. What would the credit spreads on data center builders probably do?
options: Up
Down
explain: A wider spread is the extra pay lenders demand for more risk. Data center builders lean on debt, so they would feel the worry first.

q: Before today's drop, the VIX was above 30.
options: True
False
explain: A fall of 25.83% to 26.62 means the VIX was about 36 yesterday. So fear was high before it eased.
